display_name: DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines for Business Activities Affecting Workers (2025): the Overview's list, the general principles and sections 1 to 7, as the sentences of the text that apply to an agreement, an exchange of information, an employment term or an earnings claim. Agency enforcement policy, not law.
seat: a business, or its counsel, asking what the guidelines say of an agreement with another business about workers, an exchange of information about workers, a term in its own employment contracts, or a claim it makes about workers' earnings
scope: AGENCY ENFORCEMENT POLICY, NOT LAW (n.1: it 'has no force or effect of law'): every result is a sentence of the text, with its own modal and speaker; a sentence the text states flatly is reported as what the agencies state; no result says that conduct is lawful or unlawful. Each report is a LIST of the sentences that apply, in the text's order: EMPTY when none applies on the facts given (never a finding of lawfulness), NOTHING when the answer turns on a finding not made (F23). Encoded: the Overview's list of five items and 'This list is not exhaustive' (an unnamed practice answers NOTHING, F3); the general principles (the agreement as a three-valued caller finding, F2; its form, never read; the kinds of evidence, reported, never weighed; whether the businesses compete for workers, from the labor markets each names, F1; every statement the text makes on whether an identified agreement's effects matter, with no precedence, F20); section 1 (the substance of wage-fixing and no-poach agreements, n.11; the crime and civil sentences for businesses that compete for workers and the 'illegal even if' and DOJ sentences for competing or potentially competing employers, F4; n.15 in place of 'illegal even if' on both its conjuncts, F5; the starting point, F6; the Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act sentence, F21); section 2 (franchisor and franchisee, F7; the franchisor organizing among franchisees that compete, F9; franchisees among themselves); section 3 (exchanges with businesses that compete for workers, F13; the effect sentence on a three-valued finding, F12; through a third party, F25); section 4 (non-compete clauses, F14, F18); section 5 (non-disclosure, training repayment, non-solicitation, exit fee or liquidated damages provisions and the unnamed rest, F16, F17); section 6 (the Overview's sentence on independent contractors and the competing platforms, F11); section 7 (false or misleading earnings claims, F19). Inputs, never computed: every finding (the agreement, potential competition, n.15's conjuncts, the exchange's effect, whether a term limits competition, impedes mobility or prevents the worker from leaving, whether a claim is false or misleading) and the labor markets. Not encoded: the FTC's 2024 non-compete rule and its litigation (dated, n.30-n.32), statutes and other agencies' authorities in the footnotes, section 8. No numeric inputs.

forks.F1: two businesses compete for workers when they name a labor market the same way (one shared among several is enough); products and any collaborative relationship are not read; failing that, the caller's finding of potential competition; NOTHING when either names none and there is no such finding
forks.F2: the agreement is the caller's finding with three values (identified, found none, not determined), never inferred from the evidence, which is only reported
forks.F3: non-exhaustive lists: an Overview practice the list does not name answers NOTHING; other evidence is reported as such; an agreement of a type no section speaks of gets NOTHING from the effects question
forks.F4: section 1's crime and civil sentences reach businesses that compete for workers; its 'illegal even if' and DOJ sentences reach competing or potentially competing employers
forks.F5: n.15 needs both its conjuncts and replaces only the 'illegal even if' sentence; it does not reach the crime, civil or DOJ sentences, section 2 or section 6; the general principles' collaborative relationship is not one of its conjuncts
forks.F6: the starting point gets only 'may be a form of wage fixing under the law'; the effects question gives NOTHING for it; section 6 does not read it as fixing
forks.F7: section 2's per se sentence for a franchisor and its franchisee is not conditioned on their competing for workers
forks.F9: section 2's 'franchisees that compete for workers' means actual competitors, and the franchisor's sentence also needs its organizing or enforcing; the other-laws sentence for franchisees is unconditional
forks.F10: sections 1 and 2 do not read the kind of workers (6: workers include independent contractors)
forks.F11: section 6's 'competing platforms' compete for those workers in the same labor market; the Overview's sentence on independent contractors has no condition on competing
forks.F12: section 3's effect finding has three values: found (the sentence, applied), not assessed (the sentence, pending), contrary found (no effect sentence); intent is not read
forks.F13: section 3 reads only businesses that compete for workers in the same labor market (EMPTY for potential competitors and non-competitors, NOTHING when not stated); only the sentences that say 'competitively sensitive', and the conspiracy sentence with them, need that field
forks.F14: 'that limit competition' (4) and 'that impede worker mobility or otherwise undermine competition' (5) are conditions
forks.F15: the kind of term is the caller's (a penalty on leaving is a non-compete provision in Overview item 4 and an exit fee in section 5)
forks.F16: one 'function to prevent' finding for section 5's four bullets; for training repayment, non-solicitation and exit fees the 'depending on the facts and circumstances' sentence is unconditional and 'such as if' is an example given beside it; for a non-disclosure agreement 'when' is a condition
forks.F17: 'Such provisions raise many of the same antitrust concerns' and 'may investigate if there are indications' reach the four kinds section 5 names, not the unnamed rest
forks.F18: section 4 covers non-compete clauses and section 5 every other kind; neither reads the other's findings
forks.F19: the Overview's 'false claims' sentence needs a false claim; the body's 'may investigate' sentence takes false or misleading
forks.F20: every statement on whether the effects matter that applies is listed, with no precedence among sections
forks.F21: the Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act sentence for the four roles it names reporting an antitrust crime; NOTHING otherwise; the Act itself is not encoded
forks.F22: the caller names the Overview item; the facts are read in sections 1 to 5
forks.F23: EMPTY: no sentence of the section applies on the facts given; NOTHING: the answer turns on a finding not made, or the text does not answer; neither is a finding of lawfulness
forks.F24: 'No-poach clauses in franchise agreements are also subject to antitrust scrutiny' is read for a franchisor and its franchisee
forks.F25: section 3's sentence on providing information 'through an algorithm or through a third party's tool or product' is read for any route through a third party

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the guidelines, and no independent test pass or adversarial review has been made. Every fork is assumed, not ruled (NOTES.md section 8).
